next.name: GOLD LOCUST
next.headline: GOLD LOCUST (FIN7, Carbanak): phishing loaders, the Carbanak backdoor and links to ransomware crews
next.in_short: GOLD LOCUST is tracked by Secureworks and also known as FIN7 and Carbanak. Vendors tie it to phishing-led JSSLoader attacks and the Carbanak backdoor. Some reports link its tools or affiliates to ransomware intrusions.

sentences.t: The catalogue record, sourced to Secureworks, names the actor GOLD LOCUST.
The same record lists the aliases Anunak, Carbanak, Carbon Spider, FIN7 and Silicon, and names Carbanak as its tool.
Morphisec Labs says it has tracked FIN7 (Carbanak Group) activity for several years.
Morphisec describes a JSSLoader attack chain it says it intercepted in a customer network in December 2020. It began with a phishing lure and ran VBScript stages in memory.
In that chain, a scheduled task with a timeout delay ran a module, which Morphisec says was meant to get past attack chain monitoring. A Takeout script then loaded Carbanak reflectively.
Malwarebytes attributes a late-June malspam campaign to FIN7. In a post dated August 15, 2022, it says the campaign dropped JSSLoader and a secondary .NET payload.
Malwarebytes describes this JSSLoader as a rewrite with expanded capabilities, including data exfiltration.
A report on APT28 notes that FIN7 was among several actors that used the DDE document technique, citing DNSMessenger as an example.
IBM Security X-Force reported investigating a Carbanak backdoor associated with a Sodinokibi ransomware attack. Its own text rests the Carbanak link on similarity to tools of the ITG14 group.

A SentinelLABS report published on November 3, 2022 covers Black Basta ransomware attacks. Its title says the custom EDR evasion tools are "tied to" FIN7. Only the title page and contents were available, so the detail is thin.

Rapid7, in a report published on June 10, 2025, assesses that the developers of a Java malware family are likely initial access brokers. It says they potentially provided access for Black Basta and/or FIN7 affiliates.
Rapid7 also notes that GData attributes a related python RAT to FIN7, and that GData calls it Anubis. Rapid7 says that name is likely based on the source code.
Treat unexpected invoice emails with care. Monitor script activity and scheduled tasks on endpoints, since the reported chains rely on both.
